title: Battle of Marathon
summary: Athenian hoplites defeat a much larger Persian invasion force sent by Darius I. Legend says a runner carried the news 40 km to Athens.

title: Battle of Thermopylae
summary: King Leonidas and his 300 Spartans, with several thousand allies, hold the narrow pass against Xerxes' enormous Persian army for three days before being betrayed and overwhelmed.

title: Battle of Salamis
summary: Themistocles lures the Persian fleet into narrow straits where the Greek triremes destroy it. Xerxes retreats to Asia.
significance: It saved Greek independence and opened the way to Athens' golden age.

title: Parthenon begun
summary: Under Pericles, Athens builds the Parthenon to Athena with funds from its Delian League allies — the high point of Classical Greek architecture.

title: Peloponnesian War
summary: Athens and Sparta and their alliances fight a 27-year war that ends in Athens' defeat, recorded by the historian Thucydides.

title: Trial and death of Socrates
summary: An Athenian jury condemns the philosopher Socrates to death, and he is executed by drinking hemlock. His students Plato and Xenophon wrote accounts of his trial.

title: China's Warring States period
summary: Seven powerful states fight for control of China. The era also produces Sun Tzu's 'Art of War' and the philosophies of Mencius, Laozi and the Legalists.

title: Battle of Gaugamela
summary: Alexander the Great shatters the army of the Persian king Darius III. The Achaemenid Empire falls to Macedon.

title: Alexandria founded
summary: Alexander founds Alexandria on the Nile Delta. Under the Ptolemies it becomes the greatest city of the Mediterranean, home of the Lighthouse and the Great Library.

title: Death of Alexander the Great
summary: Alexander the Great dies in the palace of Nebuchadnezzar II in Babylon, aged 32.

title: Chandragupta founds the Maurya Empire
summary: Chandragupta Maurya defeats the Nanda dynasty and founds the Maurya Empire, based in Magadha. Under his grandson Ashoka the empire controls the major cities of the subcontinent except the deep south.

title: Kalinga War and Ashoka's conversion
summary: Emperor Ashoka conquers Kalinga in a bloody war. His own rock edicts record his deep remorse; he turns to spreading Buddhist teaching (the Dharma) and sponsors Buddhist missionaries to Sri Lanka, north-west India and Central Asia.

title: Qin Shi Huang unifies China
summary: King Zheng of Qin conquers the last rival state and becomes the First Emperor. He standardises writing, coins, weights and axle widths, links the northern walls and is buried with the Terracotta Army.

title: Battle of Cannae
summary: Hannibal, having crossed the Alps with elephants, encircles and annihilates a larger Roman army — one of the most studied battles in military history.

title: Han dynasty founded
summary: Liu Bang, a peasant-born rebel, wins the civil war after the Qin collapse and founds the Han dynasty, which lasts four centuries. Most Chinese still call themselves 'Han people'.

title: Battle of Zama
summary: Scipio Africanus defeats Hannibal in Africa, ending the Second Punic War and making Rome the dominant power in the western Mediterranean.

title: Rome destroys Carthage and Corinth
summary: After a siege of nearly three years, the Roman army under Scipio Aemilianus takes Carthage and destroys it, ending the Third Punic War.

title: Zhang Qian opens the Silk Road
summary: Han envoy Zhang Qian travels west into Central Asia; his reports lead China to open trade routes that would link it with Persia and Rome — the Silk Roads.

title: Siege of Alesia
summary: Julius Caesar defeats the Gallic leader Vercingetorix, completing the conquest of Gaul.

title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
summary: On the Ides of March, senators led by Brutus and Cassius stab Caesar to death, fearing he would make himself king. The Republic collapses into civil war anyway.

title: Battle of Actium
summary: Octavian's fleet defeats Mark Antony and Cleopatra. Egypt becomes a Roman province and Octavian, as Augustus, becomes Rome's first emperor.

title: Augustus becomes first Roman emperor
summary: The Senate grants Octavian the title Augustus. Behind republican forms he founds the Roman Empire, beginning two centuries of 'Pax Romana'.

title: Crucifixion of Jesus
summary: Jesus of Nazareth, a Jewish preacher from Galilee, is crucified under the Roman governor Pontius Pilate. His followers' belief in his resurrection gives rise to Christianity.

title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
summary: Germanic tribes under Arminius ambush and destroy three Roman legions. Rome abandons its plans to conquer Germany beyond the Rhine.

title: Buddhism reaches China
summary: Tradition says the White Horse Temple, China's first Buddhist temple, is founded at Luoyang under Emperor Ming of Han.

title: Romans destroy the Second Temple
summary: Titus crushes the Jewish revolt and burns the Temple. Judaism reorganises around synagogues and rabbis, and the Jewish diaspora widens.

title: Vesuvius buries Pompeii
summary: Mount Vesuvius erupts in one of the deadliest eruptions in history, burying the Roman towns of Pompeii and Herculaneum under pyroclastic surges and ash. Excavations have revealed much about the towns and the lives of their inhabitants.

sources.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

title: Cai Lun improves papermaking
summary: The Eastern Han court official Cai Lun adds pulp from tree bark and hemp to papermaking, leading to the large-scale manufacture and spread of paper. Paper later spreads via the Arabs to Europe.

title: Roman Empire at its greatest extent
summary: Trajan leads one of the greatest military expansions in Roman history; by his death in 117 the Roman Empire reaches its largest extent. He is succeeded by his adopted son Hadrian.

title: Teotihuacan's Pyramid of the Sun
summary: Teotihuacan grows into one of the largest cities in the world, with perhaps 100,000 people living along the Avenue of the Dead.

title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
summary: A peasant uprising linked to secret Taoist societies shakes the Han dynasty. The regional generals who suppress it become warlords, leading to the Three Kingdoms period.

title: Antonine Plague
summary: An epidemic, probably smallpox, brought back by troops from the east kills millions across the Roman Empire, including perhaps the emperor Lucius Verus.

title: Sasanian Empire founded
summary: Ardashir I overthrows the last Parthian king and founds the Sasanian dynasty, Rome's great rival for four centuries.

title: Battle of Red Cliffs
summary: The southern warlords Sun Quan and Liu Bei defeat Cao Cao's fleet on the Yangtze, guaranteeing the division of China into the Three Kingdoms.

title: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
summary: Constantine defeats his rival Maxentius after, he said, seeing a vision of the cross. He becomes the first Christian emperor.

title: Edict of Milan
summary: Constantine and Licinius agree to tolerate Christianity throughout the Roman Empire, ending the persecutions.

title: Council of Nicaea
summary: Constantine calls the first ecumenical council of the Church, which adopts the Nicene Creed and condemns Arianism.

title: Constantinople dedicated
summary: Constantine dedicates Constantinople, rebuilt on the site of Byzantium, as the new eastern capital of the Roman Empire. Within half a century it is one of the largest cities in Europe and the Middle East; it remains an imperial capital until the Ottoman conquest of 1453.

title: Gupta Empire — India's 'golden age'
summary: Chandragupta I founds the Gupta dynasty. Under it Indian mathematicians develop the decimal place-value system and zero, and classical Sanskrit literature flourishes.

title: Aksum adopts Christianity
summary: King Ezana of Aksum, converted by his teacher Frumentius, becomes the first ruler of Aksum to embrace Christianity.

title: Battle of Adrianople
summary: Gothic rebels led by Fritigern overwhelm the Eastern Roman army and kill Emperor Valens. The battle is often seen as the start of the events that led to the fall of the Western Roman Empire.

title: Christianity becomes Rome's state religion
summary: Emperor Theodosius I's Edict of Thessalonica makes Nicene Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire.

title: Roman Empire permanently divided
summary: On the death of Theodosius I the empire is split between his sons: Arcadius in the East (Constantinople) and Honorius in the West.

title: Visigoths sack Rome
summary: Alaric's Visigoths sack Rome — the first time in 800 years the city has fallen to a foreign enemy. The shock inspired Augustine's 'City of God'.

title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
summary: A Roman-Visigothic alliance under Aetius halts Attila the Hun's invasion of Gaul.

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
summary: The Germanic general Odoacer deposes the boy-emperor Romulus Augustulus and sends the imperial regalia to Constantinople. Historians traditionally date the end of Antiquity here.
significance: The Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire carries on for another thousand years; in the West, Germanic kingdoms take Rome's place.

sources.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

title: Clovis, king of the Franks, baptised
summary: Clovis I unites the Franks and converts to Catholic Christianity, winning the support of the Gallo-Roman population — the seed of France.

title: Classic Maya civilisation flourishes
summary: Maya city-states like Tikal, Calakmul and Palenque build great pyramids and record their kings' deeds in a full writing system and a precise calendar.

title: Refugees settle the Venetian lagoon
summary: Fleeing Attila's Huns — and later the Lombards — people from mainland Roman towns like Aquileia and Padua take refuge on the marshy islands of the lagoon, the origin of Venice.

sources.title: History of the Republic of Venice
